title: Three legs, i
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The pup in every panel, never remarked. The strip learning a new animal's weight. He doesn't limp; he scuttles.

panels.composition: The garage. The table raised again to standing height. WOOD drawing. Under it, the braided bed — and beside the bed, not in it, BARNABY II asleep on a pile of rejected sketches he has made his own.

characters.pose: asleep on a pile of sketches beside the bed

image.prompt: a man drawing at a drafting table raised back to standing height in a garage studio, beneath it an unused braided dog bed and beside it a wiry three-legged young dog asleep on a nest of crumpled sketches, razor-sharp ink
image.notes: The old bed stays under the table, unused. The pup sleeps beside it. Never remarked.

panels.composition: The pup awake, scuttling across the room after nothing, three legs, joyful, erratic. Motion lines that owe Watterson.

image.prompt: a wiry three-legged dog scuttling joyfully across garage floorboards with erratic kinetic motion lines, not limping

panels.composition: Wood's hand, drawing the pup. Six false starts on the pad, like 1999. Then one that has the weight.
props: pad with six false starts and one right

image.prompt: close-up of a drawing pad with several abandoned sketches of a three-legged dog and one finished one that captures its balance and weight
image.notes: Rhymes with dw_1999-11-18. Six false starts, then the one.

panels.composition: The pup asleep on Wood's foot. Chewing, in his sleep, the wooden crow-quill holder. Wood drawing with a different pen.

characters.pose: asleep on his foot, nib holder in his teeth

image.prompt: a three-legged dog asleep across a man's foot under a drafting table with a wooden pen holder clutched in its teeth, the man drawing with a different pen, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: The pup's weight learned. The old bed unused. The nib holder, permanently his.
